text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are pregnant and experiencing vaginal bleeding with abdominal pain; please tell me, how many weeks pregnant are you and how long have these symptoms been occurring?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_beta_hCG (quantitative)
REQUEST TEST: Serum_BetahCG

speaker: Doctor
text:
Those beta-hCG results appear normal for the gestational age; can you describe the characteristics of the bleeding, such as the color and amount, and does the pain localize to a specific area?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: Rhesus_factor

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased), Platelets: 200,000 /μL, PT: 11 seconds, aPTT: 30 seconds, Ultrasound_Abdomen_and_Pelvis: Findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture

The ultrasound findings of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to a previous cesarean section scar, combined with hemoperitoneum and anemia, are diagnostic of uterine rupture. This is a life-threatening obstetric emergency requiring immediate surgical intervention.
